_comment: Config for the weekly sharded mutation run.
WHAT IS COVERED, AND WHY NOT EVERYTHING. `include` is the logic tier:
RunnerCore (the grading core, compiled natively AND to wasm), Core (models,
language dispatch, pattern rendering) and Worker (submission normalization,
job lifecycle). Together ~16k LOC, ~2,650 mutants, ~12h serial, which shards
to well under an hour of wall clock.
APIServer is deliberately EXCLUDED and should stay excluded. It is 94k LOC
-- 15,681 mutants -- and its mutants must be graded by APITests, the slowest
suite, so it is ~1,712h serial: about 96% of the total cost of the tree. The
value is also lowest there: it is overwhelmingly Vapor route wiring, Leaf
rendering and Fluent models, where mutants are dominated by pagination bounds
and deleted log lines. Triage cost scales with SURVIVORS, not mutants, and a
report nobody reads is worse than no report because it looks like coverage.
testArgs grades every mutant with CoreTests + WorkerTests and skips APITests.
That is a deliberate trade: including APITests would multiply per-mutant cost
by roughly 25x. The cost is that Core code reached ONLY through APITests will
show false survivors -- which is why the report tells the reader to verify
before acting, and why nothing here is a gate.
-Xswiftc -no-warnings-as-errors IS LOAD-BEARING. This package builds with
.treatAllWarnings(as: .error), and Muter's RemoveSideEffects operator deletes
the USE of a binding -- leaving `let x = ...` unused, which is a warning, which
is an error here. The mutated copy then fails to compile and the ENTIRE shard
produces zero mutants: measured, shard 0 died on RunnerDaemon+JobProcessing.swift
with six such orphaned bindings. The flag is appended after the package's own
settings and cancels them, which is the whole reason mutants can be built at all.
Do not remove it without re-running a shard containing a file whose statements
bind results -- the failure is total, not partial.
--skip ZipProcessEnvironmentTests IS REQUIRED, and the reason generalises.
Muter's PrepareSourceCode writes a preamble into every file it will mutate --
including `import class Foundation.ProcessInfo` -- BEFORE it runs the baseline
suite. ZipProcessEnvironmentTests reads Sources/Core/ZipArchiver.swift and
ZipProcessSerialization.swift and scans them for `Process(` constructions, so
the preamble trips it: one test, two files, exactly the 2 issues that made run 2
abort. A red baseline means Muter inserts NOTHING and the whole shard reports
no outcomes.
The general rule: a test that asserts on the TEXT of a file under mutation
cannot coexist with mutation, because mutation rewrites that text. Skipping is
correct rather than a workaround -- such a guard tests file contents, not
behaviour, so it has no mutants worth killing. If another source-text guard is
added over Sources/{RunnerCore,Core,Worker}, skip it here too. Guards reading
Tools/ or Public/ are unaffected: Muter only rewrites what it mutates.
